tasks.title: Tablet study group email
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Tablet study group – next steps
paragraphs: As you know, our tablet study group is planning the next session. We need to decide on the main focus. Should we use the tablets for research projects or for creating digital presentations? Which do you think is more useful for the group?
Also, we need to choose one app to try together. Would you prefer a note-taking app or a quiz app?
Finally, can you suggest one way to make sure everyone uses the tablets responsibly?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which focus you prefer (research or presentations) and explain why.
Choose an app (note-taking or quiz) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to encourage responsible use of the tablets.
Ask Mrs. Hill about the date of the next session.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Tablet study group article
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our school magazine wants to hear about your experience with the tablet study group.
What is the most useful thing you have learned by using tablets for study?
How has the tablet study group helped you with your schoolwork?
Would you recommend the group to other students? Why?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it in the next magazine!

tasks.title: Tablet study group story
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:

promptBlocks.label: Story opening
promptBlocks.text: When the programme coordinator handed out the tablets, one of them started making a strange noise.
